title: How Morton chose titles: Froggy Moore
summary: Speculation on the meaning and spelling of Froggy Moore and how Morton came by titles.

story.theme_name: How I got my name: nicknames and band monikers
story.community_name: How I got my name: nicknames and band names

blocks.x: I always get a wonderful kick out of some of the titles of Jelly's tombs, you know. You could almost write a book on the titles. I suppose that every title has a... was a stepping stone somewhere along his career.
Titles are... arrived at in a kidding way sometimes. My thought about Frog Eye Moore, you know. The real thing is Frog Eye Moore. F-R-O-G, I...
But they got Frog Eye Moore in here.
Well, that's because Sidesbust... Messed it up.
Yes. But that's right. I remember that before.

They changed that. But my belief is that some guy that played with him was... had bulgey eyes like a frog, you know. Yeah. See, and they say, oh, there's old Frog Eye there. We'll name this after him, see. Frog Eye Moore. Yes. But, what's his name? Smith in Brooklyn. He claims that Frog Eye Moore was a contortionist. Of course, that sounds plausible, you know. A contortionist does dress up like a frog very used to a long time ago. Yeah. So he could have been named after a contortionist by the name of Moore or Frog Eye.
I think your answer's better, because the original things, it wasn't Frog Eye Moore. It was not a name, Moore. It was M-O-R-E.

M-O-R-E, yeah. Well, I think this way about it. Jelly could spell, see. Yeah. Jelly could spell and he could write. And if he wanted to be Frog Eye, F-R-O-G-G-I-E, he would have spelled it to him. I think that's right. But he just did the other thing. And he wrote that in 1918, and he didn't go out to the Pacific Coast after that until 1923 when he got mixed up with Benjamin Seitz. I don't know. I always say that name wrong, whatever it is.
